candidates.name: lichen sclerosus
support_spans: Multiple hypopigmented, flat-topped papules on the back, waist, and inframammary area
folliculocentric under close inspection
central keratin plugs and some foci of structureless, whitish, and homogenous areas with surrounding erythema
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of hypopigmented, flat-topped papules with folliculocentric distribution and dermoscopic findings of central keratin plugs is consistent with lichen sclerosus.

candidates.name: keratosis pilaris
support_spans: folliculocentric under close inspection
central keratin plugs
candidates.why: The presence of folliculocentric papules and central keratin plugs could also suggest keratosis pilaris.

candidates.name: lichen sclerosus
support_spans: papillary dermis was markedly thickened with homogenized collagens, areas of edema, and sparse bandlike lymphocytic infiltration
candidates.why: The histopathologic findings of thickened papillary dermis with homogenized collagens and lymphocytic infiltration are consistent with the pathophysiology of lichen sclerosus.

candidates.name: atopic dermatitis
support_spans: pruritic papules
candidates.why: The presence of pruritic papules could suggest an allergic or atopic mechanism, as seen in atopic dermatitis.

candidates.name: lichen sclerosus
support_spans: histopathologic examination: biopsy specimen from back showed central follicular plug and epidermal atrophy covered by orthokeratotic stratum corneum
candidates.why: The histopathologic findings from the biopsy specimen are decisive in confirming the diagnosis of lichen sclerosus.

candidates.why: Dermoscopy can be a decisive modality in diagnosing keratosis pilaris, given the characteristic findings of central keratin plugs.
